passages.title: Who decides what machines learn?
passages.text: Artificial intelligence is now part of daily life. It recommends the songs we hear, translates our messages and helps doctors find illnesses earlier. Many experts call it the biggest breakthrough since the internet, but it is also one of the most debated. These systems learn from huge amounts of data, and much of that data comes from ordinary people who never agreed to share it. It is believed that some companies have used millions of private photos without asking anyone. Researchers also worry about side effects that nobody planned. A program that chooses job candidates, for example, can repeat the unfair decisions of the past if it learns from unfair examples. Because of this, it is often said that the real question is not what the technology can do, but what it should do. Some countries now require companies to explain how their systems make decisions and to protect users' privacy. Most scientists agree that the research must continue, but they want it to be ethical, open and checked by people from outside the companies.
